title: Induction of IBD by transferring CD4+ CD45RB high cells in to SCID or Rag-/- mice
protocol: Harvest splenocytes from 5 to 8 week old mice.
Incubate single cell suspensions with FITC-conjugated anti-CD4 and biotin-conjugated anti-CD45RB.
Incubate the cells with anti-FITC microbeads.
Purify CD4+ T cells by magnetic isolation using the Auto MACS sorter.
Incubate purified CD4+ T cell suspension with α-biotin microbeads for separation of CD4+CD45RB high naive cells.
Separate the cells using the Auto MACS.
Inject Thy1.2+ C.B-17 scid mice intra peritoneally with 4 × 10^5 fresh Thy1.1+CD25– CD45RBhighCD4+ congenic cells.
After 6 or 7 days, administer an i.p. injection of PBS or 0.8-1 × 10^6 freshly isolated Thy1.2+ Treg cells.
Use C57BL/6 Rag1−/− or Rag2−/− mice (CD45.1) as recipients for cell transfers.
Transfer C57BL/6 donor cells in 100 μl of PBS per mouse.
On day 6-10 after Treg cell transfer, isolate mesenteric lymph node cells or lamina propria cells using the protocol from Current Protocols in Immunology.
Perform Annexin V and Propidium Iodide staining to measure apoptosis by flow cytometry.
Conduct TUNEL staining on cryo-sections of the gut to measure apoptosis of effector cells in the lamina propria.
Analyze stained sections with confocal immunofluorescence.
